comment:paths: This package imports ITSELF by package path ~110 times, across ~30 subpaths — every one of them deliberate: tsup bundles with `bundle: true, splitting: false`, so a relative specifier inlines a private copy of the target's module state, and the full package path (paired with a matching `external` in tsup.config.ts) is what keeps it one shared copy. See that file for the per-entry rationale. Those specifiers would otherwise resolve through this package.json's own exports map, whose `types` condition points at ./dist — .d.ts files that build:types is in the middle of EMITTING, so on a clean tree every self-reference fails with TS2307 and the build cannot bootstrap. The wildcard below maps them straight at source instead, which is also what dev/vitest see (the `development` export condition serves src). Three longer patterns override it, and a longest-prefix match wins, so those are the ones tsc uses for their specifiers: `header-auth` because it is the one subpath whose name does not mirror its directory (the exports map publishes src/header/header-auth.ts at the package root), and the two `next/dynamic(() => import(...))` targets because their DEFAULT export type has to be known at the call site. Keep all of this paired with tsup.config.ts's `entry` + `external` and the exports map; all three name the same files.
